description:
Offline demonstration digital twin of ORNL's Molten-Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE, 1965-69) built on the OUTRAM PARK suite. Scope per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md: OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION / V&V / education only — no operational or live-plant coupling; MSRE is a public, decommissioned benchmark (ORNL-TM / ORNL-4xxx report series), so 'real time' means a real-time-capable simulation loop replaying/assimilating the historical record, not hardware monitoring. Data-policy clean (all MSRE data open literature).

Architecture: two-tier. OFFLINE high-fidelity (MC k-eig + depletion via outram-mc-libs+njoy; CFD via outram-foam; molten-salt Gibbs FP thermochemistry) generates reduced-order tables/models. REAL-TIME tier runs a circulating-fuel point-kinetics + 1-D loop TH (tuas/tampines, which already has FLiBe + HITEC salt correlations) + lumped Xe/FP-migration model in outram-park-digital-twin-engine (egui), with a state estimator (chem-eng real-time scaffolding) assimilating replayed MSRE data — which doubles as validation.

MSRE-specific hard physics: (1) circulating fuel => delayed-neutron precursors advect out of core (flow-dependent reactivity) - the defining effect; (2) Xe-135 gas stripping; (3) FP migration into three destinations (noble gases->off-gas, noble metals->plate on graphite/Hastelloy-N, salt-seekers->dissolved/precipitate) governed by salt redox (UF3/UF4).

Phasing: P0 zero-power circulating-fuel kinetics -> P1 add TH feedback -> P2 Xe+depletion -> P3 FP migration+chemistry -> P4 data assimilation. Each phase validates against a published MSRE dataset. All AI-assisted output is untrusted draft pending human V&V.

description:
GitHub issue #175 names these explicitly as port/parity targets, to be reproduced BEFORE any broader validation claim:
  1. effect of boundary conditions
  2. grain size and morphology
  3. sample size
  4. grain neighbourhood
  5. surface roughness / notches

V&V DOCUMENTATION HARD RULE: each case must record BOTH methodology (what is computed, the reference it is judged against, inputs, tolerances, pass criterion) AND results (measured numbers WITH uncertainty, the date and data version they were taken on, and what the result implies). A V&V test documenting only what it does is incomplete.

LITERATURE HARD RULE: catalogue the source publications in kovan-literature via 'kovan lit import' with access tier and provenance decided from the copyright page, BEFORE cataloguing. Any paper whose numbers enter the code is a dependency of this codebase; a citation pointing at nothing in the archive is a dead reference. Watch for a text-and-data-mining / AI-training reservation (see op-b7bx) — where present, catalogue metadata and factual findings only.
title: Farrer Park: reproduce upstream PRISMS-Fatigue published case studies as parity targets

description:
External blocker for op-9vo6.11 (GitHub issue #35 step 11, 'Integrate reusable kopitiam-pdf reader'). Upstream work is kopitiam#96 ('kopitiam pdf refactor for kovan'), which per its latest comment is functionally complete: all 12 phases landed (68145b9), kpdf.rs went 3899 -> 630 lines, the reusable pieces sit behind an egui feature separate from the kpdf standalone-shell feature (cargo tree verified zero eframe/rfd in an egui-only build), and there is a third-party embedding example (examples/embed_reader.rs) built by CI.

IT IS NOT PUBLISHED. Verified against the crates.io index 2026-08-31: latest kopitiam-pdf is 0.3.1, whose feature table is

    default = ["kpdf"]
    kpdf    = ["dep:eframe", "dep:egui", "dep:rfd"]

There is no separate 'egui' feature in ANY published version, so the reader extraction is unavailable to this workspace. crates/kovan/Cargo.toml:107 pins 0.3.1 (set by commit 5e504e3f, 'moved kovan to use v0.3.1 of kopitiam pdf').

NOTHING TO DO HERE FROM THIS WORKSPACE. Per CLAUDE.md's hard boundary, this workspace CONSUMES kopitiam binaries/releases only -- never a path or git dependency on a working copy, never a local patched build, never an edit or PR out of this tree. The deliverable is the upstream publish; this bead exists so op-9vo6.11 has a real blocker edge rather than a note buried in a description. Close it when a version carrying the separate egui feature is on crates.io, recording the version and the date.
title: kopitiam-pdf: publish 0.3.2+ with the reusable reader behind a separate egui feature (blocks kovan redesign step 11)

description: Incremental (or QuickHull) 3D convex hull producing a closed triangle Mesh from a set of Vec3 points. Reuse the existing robust boolean_predicates::orient3d for the orientation/visibility tests. Handle degeneracies (duplicate/coplanar points). Complements the CSG/boolean suite (bounding volumes, convex decomposition input).
title: outram-blender: 3D convex hull from a point set

description: Add STL read/write, the lingua franca for surface meshes and the standard DAGMC/Monte-Carlo feed. Export: fan-triangulate faces, per-facet normal, ASCII (to_stl_ascii) + binary (to_stl_binary) + disk writers. Import: parse ASCII/binary triangle soup into a Mesh (from_stl_ascii/from_stl_binary/from_stl_bytes with size-heuristic auto-detect); STL has no shared vertices so import returns the raw soup for the caller to weld() into topology. New stl module (I/O, not a MeshOp). V&V: cube -> to_stl_ascii/binary -> from_stl -> weld -> V8 E18 F12 chi2; binary size = 84 + 50*ntri; round-trip vertex positions preserved to f32 precision.
title: outram-blender: STL import/export (ASCII + binary)

description: Found 2026-08-11 by correlation audit during op-4542. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/parallel_heat_exchangers.rs:121-145. The equal-temperature early return computes U*A*(T_amb - T_fluid) (heat INTO fluid, matching the doc); the LMTD branch passes ambient as the cold pair and fluid as the hot pair, yielding T_fluid - T_amb (heat OUT of fluid) -- opposite sign convention between the two branches. Inline comment at L133-134 claims delta T = ambient - fluid, contradicting the actual argument order. Additionally log_mean_temperature_difference panics when hot < cold, so the function panics outright whenever ambient is hotter than the fluid -- the very heat-input case its doc describes.
title: tuas: LMTD ambient heat-flux helper has opposite sign conventions and panics when ambient hotter than fluid

description:
op-k9em.2-4 ported the scalar surface-layer and deposition kernels. The next slice is the actual Lagrangian machinery, which is where the model stops being a set of pure functions:

- advance.f90 -- the particle advection + Langevin turbulence step
- hanna.f90 / hanna1.f90 / hanna_short.f90 -- turbulence parameterisation
- cbl.f90 / initialize_cbl_vel.f90 -- convective boundary layer
- richardson.f90 -- mixing-height diagnostic

These are NOT pure scalar functions: they read com_mod global met-field state, so the Fortran reference driver must be extended to populate those arrays before calling. That is the main new work in the harness, and it is why this was not folded into the first slice.

REUSE, check before writing:
- outram-mc-libs::rng::lcg is the workspace RNG; boon-lay's lagrangian_decay_simulator already wraps it (OoRng64) and already does Gaussian sampling via central_limit_theorem/. Read that before writing any sampler -- boon-lay is genuine prior art for Lagrangian particle transport with radioactive decay in this workspace.
- petir::ode has rk4_step/rkf45_step if an integrator is needed.
- Determinism matters: a stochastic mover cannot be code-to-code verified against Fortran RNG streams directly. Verify the DETERMINISTIC parts pointwise, and the stochastic parts by ensemble statistics (mean/variance convergence) plus a fixed-seed regression fixture -- state which is which, do not blur them.

Note the Rust design rules: enums for dispatch, no Box/dyn, no lifetimes, Arc for shared field state.
title: changi: port the FLEXPART Lagrangian core (advance, Hanna turbulence, CBL)

description: outram-mc-libs' Tally struct holds filters: Vec<Box<dyn Filter>>, which violates BOTH the workspace no-trait-objects rule and the no-Box rule, and it forces the violation onto consumers: outram-blender's sim::cell_flux_tally (src/sim.rs:304) has to construct Box<dyn Filter> to use it. The filter set is closed and known at compile time, so per the workspace Rust design rules it should be an enum (FilterKind) with exhaustive match dispatch. Fix belongs in outram-mc-libs; outram-blender's call site then simplifies. Found during the 2026-08-07 outram-blender bookkeeping pass.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
outram-mc-libs SIDE LANDED, verified 2026-09-17, commit bc5516ad0617 ("mc+njoy: work the four open items..."): crates/outram-mc-libs/src/tally/tally.rs Tally.filters is now Vec<FilterKind> (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/tally/filter.rs:753), an enum, not Vec<Box<dyn Filter>>. The Filter trait remains only as the per-struct contract. grep confirms zero `Box<dyn` in outram-mc-libs itself.

NOT DONE, and this is now a live regression, not just "not yet simplified": outram-blender/src/sim.rs:330-334 (cell_flux_tally) still constructs `Box<dyn Filter>` and pushes it into `Tally.filters`, which no longer type-checks against Vec<FilterKind>.

  cargo check -p outram-blender --lib --features mc-export
  error[E0308]: mismatched types --> crates/outram-blender/src/sim.rs:334:23
    expected `FilterKind`, found `Box<dyn Filter>`

(mc-export is not a default feature, so a bare `cargo check -p outram-blender --lib` does not catch this -- confirmed the plain check is clean and the failure only appears with --features mc-export.) Not closing; the consumer this bead itself names ("outram-blender's call site then simplifies") is now broken, not merely unsimplified. Filed as a new bug, op-fk7j.

title: outram-mc-libs: Tally filters use Vec<Box<dyn Filter>> — enum-dispatch them

description:
gh:#195 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/195 — DO NOT START before op-ku5q / gh:#194 is closed and re-measured.

ORIGIN. Maintainer question 2026-09-13: is a spherical-harmonic representation helpful for rebuilding angular cross sections? Investigating it showed the ANGULAR axis already does the right thing on reconstruction, and surfaced a separate issue on BOTH axes.

THE ANGULAR AXIS IS ALREADY CORRECT ON RECONSTRUCTION (in-house precedent worth copying for op-ku5q). ENDF MF=4 stores elastic angular as Legendre coefficients (LTT=1), f(mu) = sum (2l+1)/2 a_l P_l(mu), a_0 = 1. crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/acer/angular.rs reconstructs by ADAPTIVE BISECTION to a tolerance (ANGLE_TOL; 'Maximum bisection depth when linearising a Legendre f(mu)') into a lin-lin tabulated PDF/CDF — EnergyAngular { cosines, pdf, cdf }. Harmonics as storage/reconstruction, tabulated CDF as sampling representation. Keeping harmonics to sampling is NOT wanted: a truncated Legendre series is not non-negative, hence not directly samplable.

THE ACTUAL ISSUE — interpolation BETWEEN tabulated incident energies is done in quantile space:
  thermal.rs:78-87 says so itself: 'ThermalScattering::sample picks between the
    two bracketing tables by ACE statistical interpolation. That is unbiased in
    the MEAN (it reproduces a linear interpolation of <E'> across the interval)
    but it adds a VARIANCE ... It falls as the SQUARE of the grid'
  So it is a random choice between two whole tabulations: unbiased in the first
  moment only, injects variance no number of histories removes, and does NOT
  correctly interpolate higher moments — including the width op-ku5q is about.
  acer/angular.rs:102 interpolates mean_cosine LINEARLY across incident energies,
  which is right for a moment. WHAT THE SAMPLING PATH DOES BETWEEN TABULATED
  INCIDENT ENERGIES IS NOT ESTABLISHED — needs checking; if it also picks a
  bracketing table it has the same problem.

WHY MOMENT SPACE IS BETTER. a_l(E) are smooth in E and interpolate linearly and meaningfully — a linear blend of two valid moment sets is a valid moment set, and it is the moment set of the physically interpolated distribution. Interpolating quantiles is nonlinear: preserves the mean, distorts higher moments, adds irreducible sampling variance, and its error depends on the tabulation rather than only on the physics.

PROPOSAL. Carry the moments alongside the per-energy tabulations, interpolate the moments to the actual incident energy, reconstruct the samplable law there — the same adaptive linearisation acer/angular.rs already does, performed at the sampled energy rather than at grid points.

OPEN QUESTIONS / COSTS:
  per-sample reconstruction is a build-time operation today; bisection per
    collision at ~10 Msample/s is not viable as written — needs a cheaper
    reconstruction, caching, or a precomputed family indexed by interpolated moments
  positivity must be guaranteed by any reconstruction from interpolated moments
  the ENERGY axis has no equally natural moment basis — Legendre is handed to us
    by the evaluation for angle; for S(alpha,beta) transfer it is not obvious and
    may reduce to interpolating S itself (cf. thermal.rs:278)
  IT MAY NOT BE WORTH IT: thermal.rs records the statistical-interpolation
    variance as falling as the SQUARE of grid spacing, so at 384 incident points
    it may already be negligible. NOT MEASURED against the THERMR oracle.

HARD CONDITION, same as everything else in this hunt: PRICE it. Switch the interpolation scheme behind a flag and measure against examples/graphite_kernel_vs_njoy_thermr.rs and h2o_kernel_vs_njoy_thermr.rs. Do not adopt on the grounds that moment space is the more principled representation — that is the standing lesson of gh:#193.
title: outram-mc: interpolate sampling laws between incident energies in MOMENT space, not quantile space
